conflicts.description: DOC-002's load drawing connects relay 16 to top-playfield GI (13 clear plus 13 red bulbs) and relay 26 to bottom-playfield GI (12 bulbs). Another 2-4 coin-door bulbs tap the shared F21 supply before the relay-26 contact; those unswitched cabinet lamps are supply context, not a controlled relay load. The same manual's coil table labels 16 FIELD RELAY BOT and 26 FIELD RELAY TOP; the observed R03 service labels and retained VPX LowerGILights/UpperGILights assignments agree with that table. The public trace confirms addresses and labels, not the physical region or wired bulb grouping. This is an unresolved difference a recreation consumes; neither region nor per-address quantity is promoted. Resolution path: an original-machine wired socket survey, or a physical-machine service video showing selectors 16/26 together with every bulb they illuminate, supplied by an owner or technician, must link each public address to its actual controlled playfield branch.

drivers.variant_notes: R02 CPU/sound/DMD firmware for the same AG08 cabinet, matrices, mechanisms and 128x32 DMD; alvg_dispDMD, FLIP78 and INITGAME2 fields are identical to R03.

R03 (EPC081) changes CPU, sound-program and DMD ROM images, including DMD ROM packaging; it uses exactly the same GEN_ALVG_DMD2 layout and game-data hardware fields. The unknown firmware year does not create a second physical game.

mechanisms.behavior: Two balls are supplied and installed (manual 1-3), agreeing with bsTrough.Balls=2; the driver macro's 3/*?*/ simulator parameter is not physical ball count. InitSw(17,18,0,...) puts the outhole before one monitored trough position. A drain enters the stack, 13 transfers it into the trough, and 30 ejects toward the shooter lane (21). The two coils do not directly actuate the sensors; ball movement does. Check outhole and trough jams before forcing another feed.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, two-ball trough and shooter feeder

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet shooter button 14 is held by the plunger key; output 9 fires AutoPlunger through vpmSolAutoPlungeS. The modeled plunger is pulled back at initialization. The physical shooter coil is CLL-009 on CKA-002; exact pulse and travel tuning remains recreation-owned.
mechanisms.label: Automatic shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Output 10 fires CatapultPlunger, which is pulled back at initialization. It returns a ball from the lower-left outlane when the ROM awards the feature; the outlane switch reports the ball independently. The script's solenoid-sound helper parameter is not a measured real-machine pulse width.
mechanisms.label: Left-outlane catapult / kickback

mechanisms.behavior: A ball travels through the secret-door lane (55); output 1 releases the preloaded SecretDoorPlunger. Script plunger objects implement the physical linear kicker, not a motorized door or position sensor. No door-home input exists in the printed inventory.
mechanisms.label: Secret-door kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Tunnel entry pulses 23. sw23 then destroys/transfers the ball into sw24 through a modeled subway; the Megamode stack asserts 24 while occupied and output 6 ejects from sw24 at script angle170/strength18. Those values are table tuning, not hardware measurements. Check the subway and eject cup for trapped balls.
mechanisms.label: Tunnel/subway to Megamode vertical eject

mechanisms.behavior: Three separate drop targets latch down and report their own switches. The bank's reset coil raises all three together through SolDropUp; no extra bank-down or home sensor is printed. Begin with raised targets; ROM reset coils restore them during startup/play. The retained table header reports that R03 counts four and R02 five drops toward the multiplier, but that header is an unverified ROM-behavior observation, not evidence for fitting fewer than six physical targets.
mechanisms.label: CASTLE C-A-S three-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Ball impact closes the normally-open scoring switch. The ROM controls the numbered coil; the retained table uses native VPX bumper/slingshot physics and pulses the switch, with its solenoid sound callback commented out. No mechanism home input or moving-position mark is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Left Pop Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Ball impact closes the normally-open scoring switch. The ROM controls the numbered coil; the retained table uses native VPX bumper/slingshot physics and pulses the switch, with its solenoid sound callback commented out. No mechanism home input or moving-position mark is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Right Pop Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Ball impact closes the normally-open scoring switch. The ROM controls the numbered coil; the retained table uses native VPX bumper/slingshot physics and pulses the switch, with its solenoid sound callback commented out. No mechanism home input or moving-position mark is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Left Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Ball impact closes the normally-open scoring switch. The ROM controls the numbered coil; the retained table uses native VPX bumper/slingshot physics and pulses the switch, with its solenoid sound callback commented out. No mechanism home input or moving-position mark is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Right Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Output 32 rotates Flipperdiverter away from its rest position; the retained timer returns it after 600ms. The flipper gameitem is a modeling choice for the physical ADV-001 gate. Catwalk, tower and bridge switches report ball passages, not gate position; there is no gate-home sensor. The timer is a recreation timing clue rather than a manufacturer dwell specification.
mechanisms.label: Rear catwalk/tower diverter gate

mechanisms.behavior: One dual-winding CLL-015 flipper is operated by the right cabinet button. DOC-002 draws its normally-closed local EOS contact; that high-current contact is not a matrix input. Public 45/46 are fabricated together for the whole button closure when 27 is on, and the table consumes 46 for the assembly. They do not expose independent winding currents or EOS timing.
mechanisms.label: Lower right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: DOC-002 gives the lower-left CLL-015 and upper-left CLL-003 separate coil branches with a shared left cabinet-button return. The lower-left assembly's normally-open Upper Flipper Activator (PDF44 item22, FLS-002) closes the upper branch when the lower assembly moves. Each coil has its own local normally-closed EOS contact (item24); neither contact is a matrix input. The table's SolLeftFlipper approximates this sequence by moving LeftFlipper and invisible LeftFlipper1 together. Public 47/48 are simultaneous assembly signals, not independently timed winding or upper-flipper states. To reproduce physical sequencing, model the normally-open activator from lower-flipper motion rather than inventing another controller callback.
mechanisms.label: Lower and upper left flippers
